en: If Śiva is joined with Śakti, he is able to exercise his power; if it were not so, the Lord would indeed not be capable of even a single movement.
Therefore, you are to be propitiated even by Hari, Hara, Viriñci, and the others.
How can one who has not performed meritorious deeds be able to bow down or offer praise? // Saul_1 //
Virinchi, gathering even the smallest particle born from the lotus-feet of Your feet,
creates the worlds in their entirety;
yet Śauri carries it with some difficulty upon his thousand heads.
Hara, becoming agitated, resorts to this practice of smearing himself with ashes. (Saul 2)
She is the sun for the island-city that dispels the inner darkness of ignorance;
she is the cascading stream of nectar from the blossoms of consciousness for the dull-witted;
she is the collection of qualities of the wish-fulfilling gem for the poor within the ocean of birth.
May the tusk of the Boar-form of Murāri’s enemy be for the rescue of those who are submerged. (Saul 3)

Other than you, the host of deities grants the boons of fearlessness with their two hands; you alone manifest the gestures of granting boons and dispelling fear. You exist to protect from fear and to bestow fruits that exceed even one's desires.
For indeed, O refuge of the worlds, only your two feet are truly skillful.
In ancient times, Hari, having become a woman, propitiated you— who generate the good fortune of those who bow before you— and even brought the enemy of the cities (Śiva) to agitation;
and Smara too, having bowed to you with a body to be licked by the eyes of Rati—
For even among the great sages, delusion indeed prevails within. (Saul 5)
His bow is made of flowers, his bowstring consists of bees, his five arrows are the spring season, his vassal is the Malaya breeze, and his war-chariot is the wind;
yet even so, O Daughter of the Snowy Mountain, he alone exercises an indescribable compassion toward all.
Having obtained this world from the corner of your eye, the bodiless god of love triumphs.
With her girdle-jewels tinkling, her breasts like the frontal globes of a young elephant calf, slender at the waist, with a face like the full autumn moon,
she holds in her palms a bow, arrows, a noose, and a goad.
Formerly, there was a boastful self-aggrandizement on the part of Puramathin toward us. (Saula 7)
In the midst of the ocean of nectar, surrounded by groves of celestial trees on a jeweled island containing a grove of *nīpa* trees, within a palace of wish-fulfilling gems,
upon a couch in the form of Śiva, she who dwells upon the lap of Paramaśiva—
Only a few fortunate ones worship you, the wave of the bliss of consciousness. (Saul 8)
Having pierced the entire path of the *kula*— the earth at the *mūlādhāra*, the fire situated somewhere in the *maṇipūra*,
the wind in the *svādhiṣṭhāna*, the ether in the heart,
and the mind even between the eyebrows— [he reaches the goal].
In the thousand-petaled lotus, you sport in secret with your husband. (Saul 9)
Sprinkling the phenomenal world once more with the splendor of the tradition of aesthetic essence (rasa-āmnāya), she flows as streams of nectar falling from between her two feet;
having reached her own ground, she coils like a serpent in three and a half circles.
Having made yourself your own [support], you sleep within the hollow of the family-pit.
With four Śrīkaṇṭhas, with five distinct Śivayuvatis,
and with the nine Mūlaprakṛtis of Śambhu—
thus [there are] forty-three; [along with] the petals of the earth, the digits, and the three circles of the triangle.
Together with the three lines, the corners of your feet have been transformed. // Saul_11 //
O Daughter of the Snowy Mountain, even the lords of poets, beginning with Viriñci, can somehow manage to compare your beauty;
for upon beholding it, the celestial nymphs go forth in their minds with longing.
Even the state of union with Giriśa, which is difficult to attain even through austerities.

Hundreds of women— loosening their braided tresses and casting aside the garments from their jar-like breasts— run after a man who has fallen within the range of your sidelong glance, even though he is advanced in years, harsh to the eyes, and dull-witted in jests.
The young women, their girdles suddenly snapping and their fine silken garments slipping away, [ran forth].
Those [beings] who are fifty-six on earth, fifty-two in water,
sixty-two in fire, fifty-four in air,
thirty-two in heaven, and sixty-four in the mind— these [are the six classes of beings].
Even above their rays is the pair of your lotus feet. (Saul 14)

How indeed could those who have not once bowed to you— white as the autumnal moonlight, wearing a crown of matted locks adorned with the moon, and holding a water-lily, a protective amulet, a crystal bead, and a book in your hands— remain composed?
Her speech is as sweet as honey, milk, and grapes. // Saul_15 //

O Lady who is the very wave of fresh amorous passion for the Beloved of Brahmā, only a few virtuous ones worship you— who are truly Aruṇā (the Dawn)— possessing the luster of the morning sunlight upon the forest of lotuses that are the hearts of the lords of poets.
With their profound words, these men provide delight to the virtuous.
O Mother, he who meditates upon you together with Vaśinī and the other [Śaktis], whose splendor resembles the fragments of moonstone and who are the progenitors of speech—
he becomes a composer of great poems, rendered beautiful by their stylistic turns.
With words as sweet as the fragrance from the lotus-face of the Goddess of Speech.
He who remembers you— whose bodily radiance follows the path of the splendor of the youthful sun, and by which the entire heaven and earth are submerged in crimson redness—
finds his eyes filled with the confidence of forest deer trembling in fear.
How many celestial nymphs were not brought under his control by Urvaśī? (Saul 18)
O Consort of Hara, he who meditates upon you— the digit of Love— visualizing your face as a *bindu*, the pair of breasts below that, and the half-moon of Śiva beneath them,
instantly brings even women into a state of agitation; this is exceedingly easy.
It swiftly causes even the three worlds to whirl, with the sun and moon as its pair of breasts. (Saul 19)
He who holds you in his heart— showering from his limbs a mass of rays that are like the essence of nectar— as if you were an image carved from moonstone,
quells the pride of serpents just as the lord of birds does.
She gladdens those scorched by fever with her glance, which is like a vein of flowing nectar.

With a mind that has crushed impure māyā, I contemplate Your digit seated upon six lotuses— thin as a streak of lightning and composed of the sun, the moon, and fire— within the great forest of the *mahāpadma*.
Great beings, beholding this, sustain a wave of supreme joy. (Saul 21)
"O Bhavānī, bestow upon me, your servant, a compassionate glance"—
he who desires to offer such praise and utters "O Bhavānī,
you," at that very moment, you grant him the state of union with your own self.
Her feet were resplendent, adorned by the clearly visible crowns of Mukunda, Brahmā, and Indra.
I suspect that after you had stolen his beautiful form with an insatiable mind, the other half of Śambhu’s body was also taken;
for indeed, your entire form is reddish-brown and possesses three eyes.
Bowing low with his two breasts, he wore a crown adorned with the curved crescent moon.

The Creator brings forth the world; Hari protects it; Rudra destroys it; and the Lord, concealing even his own form, withdraws it. Yet Śiva, who is eternally prior to all, bestows grace upon this entire universe.
Relying upon your command, [I shall act] while your creeper-like eyebrows quiver for a moment. (Saul 24)
O Śivā, whatever worship is performed for your two feet is indeed the worship of the three gods born of the three qualities (guṇas);
for it is performed in the vicinity of the jeweled pedestal that bears your feet.
For these [gods] stand eternally with their crowns adorned by ear-ornaments of closed buds.
Brahmā goes to the state of the five elements; Hari attains cessation;
Yama undergoes destruction; Kubera meets his end;
and even the vast, sleepless realm of Indra is closed to those whose eyes are shut.
While this great destruction prevails, that husband of yours remains. (Saul 26)
Recitation, speech, and every craft, the fashioning of mudrās, movement, the act of circumambulation, eating and so forth, the ritual of oblations,
prostration, lying down, and all pleasure— view them all through the vision of self-surrender.
May whatever playful activity I have performed become a means of honoring you.
O you who incessantly bestow upon the wretched a fortune that accords with their hopes, as you scatter the abundant nectar of your exquisite beauty—
may my mind go to this foot of yours, which is as lovely as a cluster of mandāra blossoms.
Sinking down, my life, through its organs and limbs, has attained the state of being six-legged.
Even after tasting the nectar that removes fear, old age, and death,
all the inhabitants of heaven, including Brahmā and Indra, perish;
for once one has swallowed its formidable poison, there is no reckoning with Time.
O Mother, that power of your earrings is not the root cause of Śambhu’s [destruction]. (Saul 29)
Avoid the crown of Brahmā before you;
you stumble against the hard diadem of the slayer of Kaiṭabha; cast off the crest-jewel of Indra as you proceed by force toward the palace of him to whom these [gods] bow down.
Upon your rise to power, the words of your attendants shall prevail. (Saula 30)
Having established the entire world by means of the sixty-four tantras— which are dependent on producing various supernatural powers— Paśupati remains;
yet, due to your persistent request, he has now undertaken the singular accomplishment of all human goals.
Your independent system has brought this very earth down [to the level of] the [spiritual] path.
Śiva, Śakti, Kāma, Earth, then the Sun, the Moon,
Smara, Haṃsa, Śakra, and thereafter Parā, Māra, and Hari—
these are joined at their endings with the three *hṛllekhās*.
O Mother, those castes partake in being constituent parts of your name. (Saula 32)

Having first placed this triad— Smara, Yoni, and Lakṣmī— within their minds, certain ones who delight in the flavor of eternal and boundless great enjoyment chant your name, their rosaries fashioned from the threads of the wish-fulfilling gem.
They offered oblations into the fire of Śiva with hundreds of streams of fragrant clarified butter.
O Blessed One, I consider Śambhu’s body to be yours, and your own self— O Goddess— to be the sinless self of Bhava;
therefore, this relationship of "the dependent" (śeṣa) and "the supporter" (śeṣin) exists because it is common to both.
The relationship between you two, who are devoted to the supreme bliss of the equality of flavors (samarasa), is firmly established.
You are the mind, you are the sky, you are the wind, you are the charioteer of the Maruts;
you are the waters, you are the earth—when you have undergone transformation, there is indeed nothing beyond you.
You alone, by means of your universal form, transform yourself.
O Śivayuvati, you bear a form of consciousness and bliss through your divine nature. // Saul_35 //
I bow to the Supreme Śambhu, who resides in your *ājñācakra*, who bears the splendor of ten million suns and moons, and whose sides are embraced by the Supreme Consciousness;
by worshipping him with devotion, one reaches that which is beyond the domain of the sun, the moon, and fire.
For the world dwells in darkness within the abode of light.
For the sake of purification, I worship Śiva— the progenitor of the sky— who is as pure as clear crystal, and also the Goddess, who shares in his devotion;
by the radiance of these two, as it passes forth, they follow the path of similarity to the rays of the moon.
With the inner darkness shaken off, the world shines like a female cakora bird.
I worship that indescribable pair of swans wandering in the minds of the great ones, who delight solely in the nectar of the blossoming lotus of consciousness;
from whose conversation arises the full maturity of the eighteen branches of learning.
Just as milk takes up all the qualities from water, so he takes up every virtue from his faults.
O Mother, I praise Saṃvarta, who is intent upon the sacrificial fire established within your own self-abiding state (svādhiṣṭhāna), and I praise that great Samayā;
for when the world is consumed by the great conflagration of the turbulence of his wrath, it is through her light that he burns the worlds.
Your gaze, moist with compassion, bestows a cooling treatment.

Your dark cloud-like form, whose sole refuge is Maṇipūra, is possessed of lightning in the form of the power that flashes as the adversary of darkness, and is encircled by a rainbow formed by the radiance of various shimmering jewel-ornaments.
He attended upon Hara as he rained down, while the three worlds were scorched by the sun.

I worship Navātman, the great dancer of the *mahātāṇḍava* who embodies the nine aesthetic sentiments (*navarasa*), together with his consort Samayā, intent on the dance (*lāsya*), at the root of your support;
out of compassion, for the sake of both of these [practitioners], you manifest the dual form through these two.
From those two who had found their protector, this world was born as the father and mother of Janaka. 41.
O Daughter of the Snowy Mountain, he who praises your golden crown, which is densely set with sky-jewels that have attained the state of rubies,
beholds a crescent moon variegated by the scattering of its own dark shadow within its hollow.
Why does he not fix his mind upon the bow of Śunaḥśepa?
O Auspicious One, may your mass of hair— dense, glossy, and smooth, which has surpassed a forest of blossoming blue lotuses— dispel our darkness;
for the flowers [of the world] seek to obtain its innate fragrance.
I believe that the trees of the garden of the Churner of Strength dwell within this place. (Saul 43)
May the wave of beauty of your face bestow prosperity upon us— that wave which carries fresh sunbeams as if they were prisoners of the masses of light from the intense darkness of your thick tresses.
The line of parting in her hair was like the course of a drainage channel.
Your face, surrounded by locks of hair that are naturally curved and possess the splendor of young bees, mocks the beauty of the lotus;
for when it smiles slightly, it is made radiant by the filaments of the luster of your teeth.
The honey-bees of Kāma’s eyes, intoxicated by the fragrance, revelled in them.
That forehead of yours, pure with the radiance of loveliness, shines forth;
I believe it is a fragment of the moon upon your crown. And when these two are joined together through their mutual transposition, they become one.
The full moon transforms into a plastering of nectar. // Saul_46 //
When your eyebrows, intent on shattering the fear of the world, are slightly arched,
I consider the bow of the Lord of Rati to be held by his right hand, with its string drawn by your two bee-hued eyes.
In both her forearms and her fists, Umā concealed the space between them.
Your right eye, being of the nature of the sun, produces the day;
your left eye, consisting of the lord of the night, creates the three watches of the night;
and your third gaze possesses the luster of a slightly opened golden lotus.
He enters into the twilight that moves between day and night.

Viśālā is auspicious, Sphuṭaruci is radiant, Ayodhyā is the support for the stream of compassion, Bhogavatikā is somehow exceedingly sweet, and Avantī is your gaze, which triumphs over the vast expanse of many cities.
Surely she triumphs, being fit for the conventional usage of those various names. (Saul 49)

Beholding your two ears— which never let go of the young bees that are your sidelong glances, those bees being solely devoted to the nectar of the poetic compositions of the wise— the two [bees] become agitated by the tasting of that aesthetic flavor.
Due to the influence of envy, his eyes were somewhat reddened and false. // Saul_50 //
Toward Śiva she is moist with passion; toward the faces of others, she is intent on reviling;
at the Ganges she is full of wrath; at the deeds of Giriśa she is filled with wonder; she fears the serpents of Hara; and she surpasses the beauty of the lotus.
O Mother, your gaze upon me is smiling toward your friends, yet it is filled with compassion.

These two eyes— like buds upon the crest-ornament of the lineage of the Lord of the Southern Mountain— possess lashes that, reaching to the vicinity of the ears like wings, bear the fruit of causing the melting away of the essence of tranquility in the mind of the Destroyer of Cities.
As he contemplates the graceful play of your love-god’s arrow drawn back to your ear.
O beloved of Īśāna, these three eyes of yours shine with distinct divisions of the three castes, appearing like a mixture of blue and black collyrium,
as if to create again the gods Brahmā, Hari, and Rudra who have ceased from their work.
He bore passion and goodness, as if bearing the triad of qualities beginning with darkness.
O you whose heart is devoted to Paśupati,
with your eyes— companions of compassion— that possess red, white, and dark lusters,
you surely purify this river known as the Śoṇa, the Gaṅgā, and the daughter of the Sun.
O sinless one, you bring about the confluence of these three sacred streams.
O Aparṇā, terrified by the backbiting and malice of those who whisper in your ear,
the fish surely hide within the water with their eyes fixed;
and here is this lotus, its petals closed like the panels of a door.
He leaves at dawn and enters after breaking in during the night. // Saul_55 //
"O daughter of the King of Mountains, the wise say that the world undergoes dissolution and emergence through your closing and opening of the eyes;
for this entire universe is born from your opening of the eyes and returns to dissolution."
I suspect that your eyes, free from blinking, are intent upon protecting me.
O Śivā, with your most prolonged glance, possessing the luster of a slightly opened blue lotus, bathe even me, who am far away and wretched, out of compassion;
by this he becomes blessed, and there is no loss to you on account of this.
Whether in the forest or in a palace, the moon falls equally upon all.
O daughter of the King of Mountains, for whom does your pair of curved locks not evoke the curiosity of the flower-arrowed god’s bow—
curves that shine as they extend obliquely, surpassing the path of the ears?
The lingering glance from the corner of her eye imparts the intention of aiming an arrow.
I consider this face of yours, with its pair of earrings reflected in the expanse of its quivering cheeks, to be the four-wheeled chariot of the God of Love;
mounted upon which he assails the earthly chariot that has the sun and moon as its wheels.
The great hero Māra [offered it] to Pramathapati, who had conquered him.
As Śarvāṇī incessantly drinks with the hollows of her ears the eloquent utterances of Sarasvatī— which possess the skillful grace of waves of nectar—
her cluster of earrings sways as her head moves in admiration of their wondrous beauty.
With their sharp, ringing twangs, they seemed to offer a response. (Saula 60)
May this bridge of your nose, like a silken banner atop the lineage of the Snowy Mountain,
yield for us the fruit most appropriate to our station—
bearing within it pearls formed by your exceedingly cool breaths.
By their abundance, he even outside [the city] wore pearl ornaments. // Saul_61 //
O fair-toothed one, I shall describe the likeness of the luster of your lips, which are naturally red; let the coral creeper bear fruit from this comparison,
for the *bimba* fruit is not truly red until it has acquired its hue by reflecting the glow of those lips.
How could she feel even the slightest shame in ascending the scale? (Saul 62)
As the cakora birds drank the mass of moonlight from the moon of your smiling face, their beaks became numbed by its excessive sweetness;
therefore, those with a craving for sourness [long for] the wave of nectar from your cool-rayed moon.
Night after night, they drink to their heart's content, mistaking it for sour gruel.

Victorious is that tongue of yours, O Mother, which has the luster of a hibiscus flower and performs the silent recitation (*japa*) of the repeated narration of your husband’s multitude of virtues without ceasing;
for when it rests upon his lips, it takes on the appearance of a crystal stone.
The form of Sarasvatī transforms into a body of ruby.

Having conquered the Daityas in battle, the warriors returned with their helmets removed and their armor stripped away; turning their backs on the rays of the sun, on Śiva— the destroyer of Tripura— and on discarded floral offerings,
they were like Viśākha, Indra, and Upendra, [bearing] fragments of camphor as white as the moon.
O Mother, the morsels of betel from your mouth dissolve away.
As you began to speak words of praise with your head bowed in reverence while singing various sacred legends at length,
she silenced the sweet resonance of her lute-strings with the sweetness of your own voice.
Vāṇī silently covers her own lute with her garment.

O Daughter of the Mountain, the handle of Śambhu’s mirror-like face— which is graspable by the hand, which was repeatedly lifted by the Lord of Mountains out of affection with the tip of his own hand (the snowy peak), and which was obscured by his constant preoccupation with drinking from your lower lip— has been clearly touched.
How shall we describe your chin, which is without parallel? (Saula 67)
This neck of yours, constantly embraced by the arms of the Destroyer of Cities, bears the beauty of a lotus stalk for his lotus-face;
naturally white, it is now darkened by the thick mud of black aloe-wood paste.
Beneath it, a string of pearls bears the graceful beauty of a lotus stalk.
Upon her neck, which is uniquely skilled in the melodies of the three scales, shine three lines that serve as guarantors for the number of the three-fold cords tied during marriage;
they are the source-land for various kinds of sweet musical modes.
They were like the boundary lines that define the stability of three villages.
The Lotus-born Brahmā praises with his four faces the beauty of your four creeper-like arms, which are as soft as lotus stalks,
for he is terrified by your nails from the first churning of the enemy of Andhaka.
With the intention of extending his hand of fearlessness equally toward all four heads.
O Umā, how can we describe the splendor of your hands, which mock the hue of a fresh lotus with the radiance of their nails? Alas,
let the lotus share some slight resemblance to them by even a single fraction!
If [the lotus] has petals reddened by the lac from the soles of the feet of Lakṣmī as she sports.
O Goddess, may this pair of your breasts, symmetrical and drunk upon by the elephant-faced Skanda,
with their tips constantly streaming milk, remove our distress;
for upon seeing them, the heart of that laugh-inducing one was agitated by apprehension.
Heramba suddenly touches his two jars with his hand. (Saul 72)
O banner of the Lord of Mountains, there is not even a flicker of doubt in our minds that these two breasts of yours are jeweled mortars for the essence of nectar;
for they drink from them without having known the flavor of union with a wife.
Even now, the two princes remain the crushers of the elephant-faced [Ganesha] and the krauñca bird.
O Mother, the expanse of your breasts bears a pure necklace of pearls fashioned from the frontal globes of elephants and demons,
variegated within by the luster of your bimba-like lips.
It was like the fame of you, conqueror of cities, mingled with your prowess.
O Daughter of the Mountain, I believe that from your heart flows an ocean of milk like the Sarasvatī,
which the compassionate you bestowed upon the Dravidian child for him to taste.
A lovely poet was born from among the mature poets. Saula 75.
O Daughter of the Mountain, the Mind-born (Kāma), having taken refuge in the deep lake of your navel with a body licked by the rows of flames from Hara’s wrath,
rose up from it as a streak of smoke.
O Mother, people know that as the line of hair upon you. (Saul 76)
O Auspicious Mother, that which appears to the wise as a very slender form like a ripple on the Yamunā at your thin waist is, in fact,
the space between your two jar-like breasts resulting from their mutual pressure.
Having become attenuated, it seemed as if it were entering the cavity of her navel.

O Girijā, your navel is a stable whirlpool of the Gaṅgā, a pond for the stream of the creeper-like line of hair upon the bud-like breasts, a sacrificial pit for the fire of the flower-arrowed god’s splendor, and an indescribable pleasure-chamber for Rati.
The entrance to the cave of Śiva’s eyes triumphs as the gateway to spiritual perfection.

O you whose waist has long been like the trees on the banks of a river breaking apart— your waist, naturally slender, now weary from the weight of your swelling breasts, with your body bent so that the folds at your navel seem to slowly snap asunder.
May there be well-being for you, O daughter of the mountain, who abide in the stability of equanimity.
As you fashioned your breasts— resembling golden jars— with a bodice fastened so tightly that it immediately perspired at its edges and chafed the base of your arms,
Cupid clung to them, thinking, "This will be enough to protect them from being broken."
O Goddess, it is bound in three ways by the three folds [of your waist], like the creepers of the lavalī plant.
O Pārvatī, the Lord of Mountains, having severed his own weight and breadth from his hips, deposited them upon you in the form of an ornament;
therefore, this vast and heavy [girdle] of yours encompasses the entire earth.
The fullness of her hips conceals it and brings about lightness.

O Daughter of the Mountain, with both your well-rounded thighs— firm from bowing before your husband— you have surpassed both the trunks of lordly elephants and the clusters of golden plantain stalks.
With his two knees, he even conquered the pair of frontal globes of the elephant of the gods.
O Daughter of the Mountain, the God of the Uneven Arrows (Kāma) has indeed rendered your two calves into quivers containing double the number of arrows in order to defeat Rudra;
for at their tips, ten arrow-heads are seen upon each pair of feet.
Having the guise of fingernail-tips, they were sharpened solely on the whetstone of the crowns of the gods.
O Mother, place with compassion upon my head those two feet which the crest-ornaments of the Vedas bear as their crowning glory;
for the water used to wash those feet is the river that flows from the mass of matted hair of Paśupati.
The beauty of lac-dye and the luster of the reddish crest-jewel [of Śiva] belong to those two.
We offer our salutation to this pair of your feet, so pleasing to the eye and adorned with clearly radiant red lac,
which intensely resent being struck and yet long for that very blow.
The Lord of Creatures [dwelt] at the *kaṅkeli* tree in the pleasure grove.
Having uttered a false slip of the tongue regarding his lineage, she strikes her husband on the forehead with her lotus-feet, which are bent in embarrassment; thus,
after a long time, she has uprooted the internal dart caused by that burning shame.
With the clanging of his golden anklets, the enemy of Ishana let out a triumphant shout of joy.
Capable of destroying the great snowfall and adept at traversing the slopes of the snowy mountains,
they are radiant both during the night and in the latter part of the day;
they are the supreme vessel of fortune, bestowing prosperity upon those who observe the sacred times.
O Mother, it is a wonder that your two feet surpass the lotus; what is strange about this? (Saul 87)
O Goddess, how have your feet— the very abode of beauty and the refuge from calamities— been compared by the wise to the hard shell of a tortoise?
Or rather, how were they held in the arms by the Destroyer of Cities at the time of his marriage?
That which was placed upon the grindstone by him with a compassionate heart.
O fierce goddess, your feet seem to mock the celestial trees with their nails— which are like moons causing the lotus-hands of the women of heaven to close—
as they bestow fruits upon those who stand firm by means of the tips of their sprout-like hands.
To the poor, they grant auspicious prosperity incessantly and without delay. // Saul_89 //
O Mother, tell me at what time may I, seeking knowledge, drink the water used for washing your feet, which has been colored with lac-dye,
and which serves as the cause of poetic inspiration even for those who are by nature mute?
That which she places upon her lotus-like mouth becomes the flavor of betel.
Intent as if to begin the practice of the sport of setting down their steps,
those domestic swans do not cease their playful movement;
they have mastered the art of graceful striding, accompanied by the charming tinkling of jeweled anklets.
To him who was speaking deceitfully of his lotus-feet, O you of beautiful conduct! (Saul 91)
Curved in her hair, naturally straight in her gentle smile;
like the *śirīṣa* flower in luster, yet as hard as stone upon the slope of her breasts;
exceedingly slender at the waist, yet broad across the expanse of her bosom.
Victorious is a certain ruddy compassion of Śambhu, which protects the world! (Saul 92)
You belong to the inner sanctum of the Enemy of Tripura; therefore, the limit of service to your feet is difficult for those of restless senses to attain.
For it is thus that these [gods], headed by Indra, have been led to incomparable perfection.
The immortals [are surpassed] by your powers, such as *aṇimā*, which stand at the very threshold of your door.
Those who are sustained by Brahmā, Hari, Rudra, and Īśvara have become your couches;
Śiva himself serves as the deceptive coverlet, fashioned from the reflection of your own pure radiance, which has turned it crimson by receiving the rebound of your splendors.
The embodied Śṛṅgāra, like the aesthetic sentiment itself, yields curiosity for the eyes.
The moon’s spot is musk; its orb is composed of water;
its digits are camphor, packed within an emerald casket.
Therefore, by your enjoyment, this hollow interior becomes empty day after day.
Fate surely thickens its bonds for your sake again and again. (Saul 95)
What wonder is there for him who, meditating constantly upon You as "I," serves You eternally with the rays of light— such as *aṇimā* and the rest— emanating from his own body,
while he regards the splendor of the Three-Eyed One as a mere blade of grass?
The great fire of universal destruction performs the rite of lustration.
How many poets do not resort to the wife of Brahmā?
Or who does not become the husband of the goddess Śrī through whatever riches? Yet, O virtuous lady, you are the last among chaste women to have abandoned Mahādeva.
Even the clinging of breasts to a *kuravaka* tree is difficult to obtain.
Those who know the scriptures declare the Goddess of Speech to be the consort of Brahmā,
Padmā the wife of Hari, and the Daughter of the Mountain the companion of Hara;
yet you are some fourth being, whose boundless majesty is difficult to comprehend.
O Great Illusion, O Consort of the Supreme Brahman, you cause the universe to wander in delusion.
May he, who rivals Brahmā and Viṣṇu through Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī,
and who loosens the devotion of Rati toward her husband with his charming form—
may he live long, having destroyed the entanglement of the bonds of animal existence.
One who devotes themselves to you experiences the essence known as the Supreme Brahman.
The rite of waving lights for the Maker of Day is performed by the flames of lamps;
the preparation of the respectful offering (arghya) for the Moon, the progenitor of nectar, is made with droplets of water from moonstones;
and the act of satiating the ocean is accomplished by its own waters.
O Mother, this praise of your words is accomplished by means of your own words. (Saula 100)
The sun-gem, brought by its own feet to the state of a jeweled mirror,
remains smooth with its rays held steady within out of fear; it bears your face reflected therein, forever blooming without fatigue.
He was like the moon, free from all fear, [entering] his own heart-lotus.

The god of love, his body possessing the luster of a blossoming kadamba tree, produced in the mind of Hara the delusion that you were present— [Hara] whose chest bore the weight of full, swelling breasts and who possessed a beautiful smile and side-long glances.
O Umā, this is the fruition for those who are devoted to you. (Saul 102)
O Eternal One, ever-smiling, possessed of boundless virtues, skilled in ethics, whose knowledge is unassailable, the sole abode of disciplined minds devoted to restraint;
liberated from destiny, You are the object of praise for all the Upanishads.
O You who are free from fear and eternal, bring this hymn of praise to me as well to its conclusion.
